paper.subject: geography
paper.title: 1996 iGeo – The Hague, The Netherlands Multimedia Test - Questions

transcription.verifiedBy: mechanical:textlayer+regions (mechanical check only: schema, text layer, printed figures; no second model, prompt mech-v1)
transcription.notes: The paper prints three themes (Theme Maps, Theme Water, Theme Regional geography), each with three multiple-choice questions numbered 1–3; the archive inventory lists 4 top-level problems (it splits Theme Maps question 2 off as a separate entry). Each theme is transcribed as one problem with its three questions as parts (9 parts in total). No points and no time limit are printed. The name 'Thyne' in Theme Maps question 3 is printed so (the maps say River Tyne); names are never changed, kept verbatim. The misspelling 'diagarms' in Theme Maps question 1 was fixed to 'diagrams' (tx.edits). Figure lettering in the GNP graph ('Growth GNP per capital', Dutch 'voorspelling') is part of the figure. The answers document gives only the letter of the correct choice for each question.

figures.alt: Cartogram of rectangles sized by country, with an equator-like dash-dot line; labelled boxes include U.S.A., U.K., France, W. Ger., U.S.S.R., Ch., Jap., IND, Ita., Sp., Me., Br., Arg., Aus. and many small unlabelled or abbreviated boxes.
Topographic contour map of a landscape with deeply incised meandering valleys; contour values such as 1,000 and a scale bar labelled One mile in the upper right corner.

Two sketch maps, Map 1 and Map 2, each showing the River Tyne flowing east to the coast with a shaded circular city area; in Map 1 the circle lies further upstream, in Map 2 it straddles the river nearer the coast. Each has a north arrow (N) and a scale bar 0–5–10 km.

parts.statement:
What is shown in this diagram? (analysing diagrams)

a. Gross national product
b. Oil production
c. Agricultural production
d. Number of inhabitants

Which is the best characterisation of this landscape? (analysing maps)

a. Plain
b. Table land
c. Low mountains
d. High mountains

Newcastle is at the lowest bridging point on the Thyne, and stands on its northern bank. The city covers a roughly semi-circular area extending for four kilometres in all directions. Across the river lies Newcastle's twin - Gateshead - covering about half the area of Newcastle.

Which map fits the description in the text? (analysing maps)

a. Map 1
b. Map 2
c. Both maps
d. Neither of the two maps

figures.alt: Sketch of a winding river channel with four cross-lines labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4; at line 3 the channel is widest and contains a small island.

Climate diagram: monthly precipitation bars (left axis mm, 0–400) and a temperature curve (right axis °C, −10 to 30) for months J F M A M J J A S O N D; temperature peaks near 28 °C in July, precipitation is low in summer and highest in October–December.

Three block diagrams of river landscapes labelled 1, 2 and 3: 1 a wide flat valley with a meandering river; 2 a plateau with a waterfall step and a braided channel; 3 a steep mountain valley with a narrow river.

parts.statement:
At which point can the river be most easily crossed? (analysing maps)

a. At 1
b. At 2
c. At 3
d. At 4

Which town does the climate diagram refer to? (analysing maps)

a. Los Angeles
b. Shanghai
c. Cape Town
d. Buenos Aires

Which are the consecutive stages that a river goes through? (analysing maps)

a. 1,2,3
b. 1,3,2
c. 3,2,1
d. 2,3,1

figures.caption: The rock of Gibraltar
figures.alt: Black-and-white photograph of a cargo ship sailing in front of the Rock of Gibraltar.

Line graph of growth of GNP per capita (vertical label 'Growth GNP per capital', axis 0–80) against years 1965–2000, with a 'voorspelling' (forecast) marker; line 1 dashed rising steeply to about 70, line 2 roughly flat around 20, line 3 low near 0 rising slightly to about 10.
Two black-and-white photographs: above, women selling food at street stalls beside parked cars; below, a man in shirt and tie standing in an office in front of a wall map and a framed portrait.

parts.statement:
In which direction is the ship sailing? (analysing pictures)

a. Red Sea
b. Persian Gulf
c. Mediterranean
d. Atlantic Ocean

Which of the legends of the diagram is correct? (analysing diagrams)

a. 1 NIC, 2 Debt owing countries, 3 Africa
b. 1 NIC, 2 Africa, 3 Debt owing countries
c. 1 Debt owing countries, 2 NIC, 3 Africa
d. 1 Africa, 2 Debt owing countries, 3 NIC

Which country is shown in the pictures? (analysing pictures)

a. Ukraine
b. Kyrgyzstan
c. Canada
d. Pakistan

solution.statement:
Theme Regional geography

1. d
2. a
3. b
